title: Exception Hub: unified failure signal gateway and SLO root visualizer
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Teams struggle to correlate model-layer failures with transport and infra signals. Timeouts, overload conditions, model execution errors, and HTTP/gRPC codes are surfacing in separate tools (traces, logs, metrics) and require manual stitching during incidents. This ticket creates an "Exception Hub": a single logical gateway that ingests enriched failure signals from tracing hooks, metrics and log pipelines, and emits normalized failure events to dashboards and SLO calculators.

Goals:
- Define a canonical failure taxonomy that covers timeout variants (client, network, model-kv-cache), overload/backpressure, model errors (OOM, invalid logits, generation abort), and transport errors (HTTP 4xx/5xx, gRPC UNAVAILABLE/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED).
- Implement a lightweight failure enrichment pipeline converting traces/logs/metrics into normalized failure events with attributes: failure_class, stage (ingress, runtime, egress), model_variant, region, route, latency_ms, token_count, and http_grpc_code.
- Wire the enriched events into a new dashboard and SLO root visualizer that lets oncall pivot from a failure class to example traces, top offending routes, and the contributing upstream (scheduler, model-serving, infra).
- Provide an automated mapping for alerting: map failure_class -> SLO action (page, ticket, suppressed) with severity and suggested remediation playbook link.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical taxonomy doc published and approved by SRE/Model-serving/Platform (Confluence link)
Trace and log enrichment stage deployed in staging, producing normalized failure events with expected attributes for 95% of sampled faults
New Failure Insights dashboard (console) shows: failure-class breakdown, latency distribution by class, top 10 routes by failure rate, and example trace links
SLO visualizer can filter by failure_class and surface per-route error budget consumption with a one-click drilldown to the top 5 traces
Alert mapping rules added to alerting repo and tested with synthetic injection; pager suppressed for low-severity model-rejection errors
Migration plan for legacy dashboards described and scheduled; no more than 2 concurrent dashboards showing contradictory metrics after rollout
implementation_notes: Tracing hooks: add a failure tag enrichment in trace-adapter that classifies timeouts (client vs runtime), overload (backpressure hint), and model errors (capture model-exec error codes). The hook should be safe-fail and add minimal latency (~100us).

Metrics/log pipeline: create a new enrich stage in telemetry-pipeline that consumes trace/span logs + model-serving logs and emits JSON failure events to the events topic (kafka: telemetry.failures). Use deterministic keys (route+model_variant+hour) for partitioning.
Normalization rules: implement a small ruleset (yaml) that maps raw error signals to failure_class. Example rule: gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED + 'queue-full' -> failure_class: overload.queue_capacity

Sampling: high-signal errors (5xx, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, OOM) should be sampled at 100%; soft-failures (user-timeout, client-cancel) sampled at 10% by default. Provide a fast-path to increase sampling for active incidents.

Dashboard design: left panel failure-class trend, center latency violin per class, right top-routes table with sparkline and sample trace links. Add an interactive SLO root visualizer to correlate error-budget burns to failure classes.
Privacy/compliance: scrub PII in sample traces before sending to the dashboard; reuse existing scrubbing lib (github PR linked).
Fallback: if enrichment pipeline is down, dashboards should surface raw metrics with a banner and provide a link to degraded runbook.
